# KeMeK PDF Lab

> A privacy-first PDF toolkit that runs entirely in the browser — merge, split, reorder, rotate, watermark, number, fill & flatten forms, extract text and images, convert pages to images, and open password-protected PDFs. No signup, no tracking, no upload: files never reach a server.

KeMeK PDF Lab is a static, 100% client-side web app — there is no backend, so documents are processed in the browser tab and never transmitted or stored. Exports are metadata-clean by default: the source file's author, dates and XMP are dropped (page-level metadata and photo EXIF included), and only a neutral "KeMeK PDF Lab" producer tag is added (no user data, no timestamp). The tool is free, open source (MIT-licensed), and part of the KeMeK Tools suite.

## Use it
- [KeMeK PDF Lab](https://pdf.kemek.com): the live app — drop a PDF (or JPG/PNG image) and start.

## What it does
- Merge multiple PDFs into one; reorder pages by drag-and-drop; rotate, delete and label pages.
- Split into separate files — each page, fixed-size chunks, or just the selected pages (downloaded as a ZIP).
- Watermark (text or image, positioned or tiled), page-number and header/footer stamps, and click-to-place text overlays — all burned in on export.
- Sign: draw, type or upload a signature and place it on any page.
- Fill AcroForm fields; they stay fillable in the export unless flattened (locked).
- Inspect what metadata a PDF carries; strip it on export (the default).
- Extract selectable text to .txt (reading order) and embedded images to a ZIP; export pages as PNG or JPEG.
- Open password-protected PDFs — decrypted in the browser at load time, never sent anywhere.

## Source & licensing
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/kemeknetwork/kemek-pdf-lab): MIT-licensed. The whole app is client-side, so the source is exactly what runs — you can audit that nothing is uploaded.
